trust_decision.summary: Not decided anywhere: a jail-internal path is checked only lexically for '..' and then joined onto the jail root, so the plugin trusts that no component inside the jail is a symlink; the resulting host path is subsequently mkdir'd/mv'd (and read) as root outside any jail confinement.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names put_file and the host-side root mv, and this is the only place in the repository that runs a host-side mkdir/mv on a path derived from a jail-internal destination.

fix_sites.entry_point: _jail_path, the internal mapping helper shared by put_file and fetch_file

O3_reason_to_dismiss: fetch_file reaches the host through the inherited scp/sftp transport as the plain SSH user rather than under doas/sudo, so a solver can call it a read-only vector and say the advisory is about put_file's root mv.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: ansible_jail_root is documented for nested/VNET jails where the configured root may itself be reached through a host symlink, and in-jail paths legitimately contain symlinks that stay inside the jail; a fix that rejects every symlink component, or that compares realpath(dest) against the un-resolved configured root, breaks every transfer in those setups.

O6_input_shapes: absolute destination path (the normal copy/template shape)
relative destination path (lstrip('/') at jailexec.py:286 strips all leading slashes)
destination directory that does not exist yet and must still be created by mkdir -p
intermediate path component that is a symlink pointing out of the jail root
final component that is an existing symlink or existing regular file (overwrite)
put direction vs fetch direction of the same mapping
jail root from the jls probe vs the ansible_jail_root override

O8_uncovered_routes.route: put_file's 'mkdir -p <dest_dir>' half runs on the jail host as root before the move and follows a symlinked intermediate component, creating directories outside the jail even if the mv target is guarded
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the mv as the sink, so the mkdir reads as setup, and a guard applied to the mv destination looks like it covers the same command.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, three lines above the mv

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a put_dir/directory-sync helper that stages a tarball and extracts it into the jail, re-implementing the staging + root-side mkdir/mv primitive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer extending a connection plugin past single-file copy naturally adds directory transfer, and it would build its own path join and its own extract command rather than reuse put_file's guard

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second fetch_file transport branch (piped/dd instead of scp/sftp) that reads the host-side path through a different code path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the inherited SSH plugin supports several transfer methods, so a per-method branch is a natural addition and each branch needs the confinement check independently

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a rollback/cleanup helper that removes a caller-supplied destination under the jail root as root after a failed transfer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the existing failure path already runs 'rm -f' as root; extending it to remove the partially written destination is an obvious improvement that repeats the same unchecked path mapping

O9_family: CWE-59 link following / symlink-mediated jail escape on host-side file transfer (CWE-22 path confinement adjacent)

O10_build.toolchain: pip/setuptools (setup.py), pytest + pytest-cov; flake8/black/isort/bandit in CI
O10_build.project_tests: Unit suite under tests/ (CHANGELOG.md:30 claims 62 tests) stubs the SSH base class with unittest.mock (tests/conftest.py:57-63), so it runs offline; pytest.ini:14 enforces --cov-fail-under=100; the integration smoke test needs a real FreeBSD jail host and is continue-on-error in CI (.github/workflows/integration-test.yml:60-63).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the mv in put_file (a realpath/test -L check or a rename-based trick), leaving the mkdir -p half, the shared _jail_path and fetch_file as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: The plugin inherits its transfer machinery from the ansible-core ssh plugin, which is not part of this repository and was not examined.
unverified: The supplied fix diff (scr-2975.fix.diff) contains only the merge-commit header for 6e80eec with no hunks, so fix_sites, O1, O2 and O6 are inferred from the pinned code and the advisory summary rather than read from the patch.

Whether the published fix also guarded the mkdir half and how it handled a destination directory that does not exist yet is unknown; O8.present_in_latest is unknown because the input states no latest release was provided.
End-to-end symlink behaviour needs a FreeBSD jail host; offline the suite can only assert on the command string passed to the stubbed SSH base class (tests/conftest.py:57-63).
Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell in this session); jailexec.py is 336 lines and the tests about 700 lines, far below the 5 MB tiny_repo threshold.
The candidate record's counts (c_fix_sites=8 in one file, c_same_check_sites=2) were used only as a sanity check, not as evidence.
